clue.text: Living off others is a trap I worry about

indicators.note: to worry something is to tug and toss it about, so the letters before it are shaken into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A warning that sponging off other people is a trap the speaker frets over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worry about' reads as one phrase, but 'about' is split off to give the circa abbreviation, tacked on after the shuffled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasitic creature or person feeds on a host, drawing its sustenance from them without giving back.

clue.text: Searches for fancy spur set in diamonds, for example

indicators.note: something fancy is elaborate or ornamented, so the word after it is dressed up in a new order

blocks.note: rearranged, though one of its letters has to be shared with the next piece
diamonds is one of the four suits in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Someone hunts for a decorative spur studded with diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: Shuffling SPUR gives PURS, and PURS + SUITS would be nine letters; the setter lets the S of SPUR double as the S starting SUITS, a slip.
explanation.definitionFit: Pursuits are chases or quests, so the plural noun matches searches in the sense of hunts after something.

clue.text: Perch on rotten torso

indicators.note: something rotten has decayed and fallen apart, so the word after it is broken up and reformed

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something, perhaps a bird, settles on a decaying body.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost is a place where a bird settles to rest, and as a verb it means to settle on a perch.

clue.text: Lengthy tale in which woolly-headed Conservative follows hounds

indicators.note: follows tells you the party is placed after the animals rather than before them

blocks.note: a woolly head of hair is a shaggy one
hounds are hunting dogs
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A long anecdote in which a dishevelled Tory politician trails behind a pack of hunting hounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woolly-headed' looks like it means muddled, but here it describes hair. Tory is the everyday name for a British Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaggy dog story is a long rambling joke or anecdote with a deliberately pointless or feeble punchline.

clue.text: Quiet holy man sits in middle of row - he knows the form

indicators.note: sitting in the middle of something means being placed inside it, splitting the outer word in two

blocks.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
ST is the abbreviation for saint
a tier is a row of seats, one above another

explanation.surface: A silent clergyman takes a seat halfway along a row, an expert on the form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The form' sounds like a document, but in racing it is a horse's record of past results, which a tipster studies.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipster sells predictions on races, drawing on knowledge of each runner's recent record of performances.

clue.text: Mild student covered with plaster

indicators.note: being covered with something means being wrapped inside it, so the learner goes inside the building material

blocks.note: cement is a binding plaster-like building material
L is the learner plate, a crossword student

explanation.surface: A gentle student ends up coated in plaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement weather or temperament is gentle and merciful, the same sense as calm, soft conditions.

clue.text: Winter weather's here

blocks.note: the apostrophe-s is used as the letter itself
here as in at this point, as in the phrase here and now

explanation.surface: An announcement that the cold season's weather has arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s looks like a contraction of 'is' but just supplies its letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Snow is the frozen precipitation that falls in the coldest season of the year.

clue.text: Troublemaker went to Suffolk town

indicators.note: to trouble something is to stir it up, so the following letters are disturbed and rearranged

blocks.note: the last five letters of the first word, after the signal, plus the whole second word

explanation.surface: A troublemaker headed off to a town in Suffolk, an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Troublemaker' reads as one word, but it splits into the anagram signal and the first half of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Newmarket is a town in Suffolk, an eastern English county, famous as the home of British horse racing.

clue.text: Dig around in rain to find device

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are turned about into a different order
in places the rearranged letters inside the word for wet weather

blocks.note: rain is wet weather, and wet can mean rain
rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone digs about in the rain hunting for a gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A widget is a small gadget or mechanical device, often one whose name is not known.

clue.text: Documentaries about German capital causing gloom

indicators.note: a capital is a head letter, so only the first letter of German is taken
about suggests turning things around, so all the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
its first letter

explanation.surface: Documentaries on Berlin leave viewers feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German capital' looks like Berlin, but capital here just means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Discouragement is a loss of confidence or hope, a downcast state close to gloom or dejection.

clue.text: Brazilian city gets German agreement to make wine

blocks.note: Rio de Janeiro, usually just Rio
ja is German for yes

explanation.surface: A deal struck between Rio and Germany produces a wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red or white Spanish table wine from the region of the same name in northern Spain.

clue.text: Travelling rep comes to see editor seen before

indicators.note: travelling means moving about, so the word after it changes position letter by letter

blocks.note: rearranged
to view is to see
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A travelling sales rep calls on an editor he has met before.
explanation.definitionFit: Something previewed was shown or watched in advance, ahead of its general release to the public.

clue.text: Uneasy over bird swallowing gramme of heroin

indicators.note: a bird swallowing something takes it inside, so the abbreviations go into the bird

blocks.note: the time is up when it is over
a tit is a small songbird
g is the abbreviation for gramme
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A nervous bird gulps down a gram of heroin.
explanation.definitionFit: Uptight is informal for tense and anxious, unable to relax, much as uneasy describes discomfort.

clue.text: Valence transported to a cut-off part of the country

definitions.text: a cut-off part of the country

indicators.note: transported means carried somewhere else, so the letters are moved into new places

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone from Valence, a French town, is moved to an isolated region.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclave is a territory wholly surrounded by foreign land, separated from the rest of its own state.

clue.text: Astonished when Rolls runs into lorry

blocks.note: to roll like a drum is to thunder
lorry is the British word for truck

explanation.surface: Shock at a Rolls-Royce car crashing into a lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital R makes Rolls look like the car, but it is the verb, as thunder rolls; a lorry is the British name for a truck.
explanation.definitionFit: Thunderstruck means stunned with amazement, as if hit by a sudden bolt from the sky.

clue.text: Dunce sent out, having no sense of smell

definitions.note: strictly the answer means having no smell rather than unable to smell

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are thrown out of their places and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A slow pupil is sent out of class, apparently lacking even a nose for things.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on sense of smell: the answer means free of scent, not unable to detect one.
explanation.definitionFit: Unscented products carry no added fragrance or perfume, so they give off no odour at all.

clue.text: Kohl takes look at big ship

blocks.note: to eye something is to look at it
an ocean liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: Kohl, perhaps a Chancellor, goes to see a great ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Kohl is capitalised to suggest Helmut Kohl, the German chancellor, but it is the dark cosmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Kohl is a black powder used around the eyes, a traditional kind of cosmetic for lining them.

clue.text: Importantly, make some sign if I can't lynch him

indicators.note: some means only a portion of the following words is used

blocks.note: a run of letters across these words

explanation.surface: A lynch mob member who can't bring themselves to do it is urged to signal instead.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through almost the whole phrase, stopping two letters into lynch.
explanation.definitionFit: Significantly means in a meaningful or notable way, matching importantly as a sentence adverb.

clue.text: Island taking legal action on broadcasting

blocks.note: IS is the abbreviation for island
suing is bringing a lawsuit

explanation.surface: An island community goes to court over a broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Issuing means putting out or giving out publicly, as broadcasting sends out news or programmes widely.

clue.text: Innocent girl at home has information on undesirable extremes

indicators.note: extremes are the two ends, so only the first and last letters are kept

blocks.note: someone at home is in
gen is British slang for information
its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A naive young woman at home learns about the worst of things.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen is informal British slang for the facts or information.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingénue is a naive young woman, especially the stock character of one in a play or film.

clue.text: Account with American money causes stress

blocks.note: AC is the abbreviation for account
a cent is a US coin, a hundredth of a dollar

explanation.surface: Dealing with a dollar account gives someone anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stress' suggests worry, but it is the emphasis placed on a syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: An accent is the emphasis given to a syllable or note, the same thing as stress in speech.

clue.text: Devises a secret process

indicators.note: to process material is to work it over, so the words before it are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone invents a hidden method.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Process' looks like a noun, a method, but works as a verb telling you to work the letters over.
explanation.definitionFit: To create is to devise or invent something, bringing a new thing into being.

clue.text: Happy to find shelter in stormy gulf

indicators.note: stormy waters are churned up, so the following letters are tossed about
in places the word for shelter inside the rearranged sea letters

blocks.note: rearranged
the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: Relief at finding shelter from a storm at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Gleeful means full of delight or high spirits, a merry state of joy.

clue.text: University guest losing way following loud piece of music

indicators.note: following puts the university and guest letters after the music sign for volume
losing means the abbreviation for a street is dropped from the visitor

blocks.note: f, forte, is the musical direction for loud
U is the abbreviation for university
taken as written
ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: A visiting academic who gets lost follows a loud bit of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing way' sounds like getting lost; it means removing ST, the abbreviation for street.
explanation.definitionFit: A fugue is a contrapuntal composition in which a theme is taken up by successive voices in turn.

clue.text: Old lover has wrong semi-notion of blackmail

indicators.note: semi means half, so only half of the word that follows is kept

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
a tort is a civil wrong in law
taken as written, then halved

explanation.surface: A former partner has a twisted half-idea about blackmail.
explanation.walkthrough: A tort is the legal term for a civil wrong; the back half of notion is kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Extortion is obtaining money by threats or force, of which blackmail is the classic example.

clue.text: Scottish town has the Spanish spirit

blocks.note: el is Spanish for the
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A Scottish town enjoys a Spanish liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: Elgin is a town in Moray in northeast Scotland, known for its cathedral ruins and nearby whisky distilleries.

clue.text: Cartoonist Bill is neat

blocks.note: first meaning: Bill ..., a British newspaper and magazine cartoonist
second meaning: orderly, in good order

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain cartoonist is well groomed.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill Tidy was a prolific British cartoonist, known for Punch and Private Eye strips.
explanation.definitionFit: The cartoonist's surname is also the everyday adjective for orderly and well kept.

clue.text: Plough new bare earth endlessly after first gleaning

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the following word is taken
without an end, the final letter of the soil word is dropped
new suggests the letters are made over into a fresh order
after puts the reworked letters behind the single letter taken from the farm word

blocks.note: its first letter
taken as written
taken as written, then cut short

explanation.surface: Farm work: ploughing bare soil once the gleaning is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plough' looks like a farm verb, but it is the British name for the star pattern within the Great Bear.
explanation.definitionFit: The Plough, called the Big Dipper in America, is the best-known star group in the constellation Ursa Major.
